subject: URGENT: Atlas Dynamics - retention signoff & nonstandard concessions request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Atlas Dynamics - retention signoff & nonstandard concessions request

Team,

We need executive signoff to close a renewal by end-of-week for Atlas Dynamics (Deal DL-2028-013). They've given an explicit walk timeline: if we don't provide terms that match competitor counteroffer they will move to a 3rd-party provider. This is a high-visibility account (AI-driven logistics, $2.1M ARR).

Customer ask (summarized):
- 25% subscription discount on first 12 months (applied to current committed ARR of $600k for the upcoming contract year)
- One-time credit of $150,000 for migration/training hours (customer cites integration work and data egress costs)
- Reset contract term to a new 12-month start-on-signature date (they are mid-term and want alignment with fiscal year)
- SLA addendum to 99.9% with service credit ladder and a quarterly operational review commitment from CS

Why this matters:
- Atlas is strategic: public case study potential, multiple product teams with future expansion potential, and an embedded partner introduction pipeline.
- Risk: Procurement has a competing priced offer with an aggressive first-year discount plus free onboarding hours.
- Upside: Committing to the requested bridge terms with a 12-month renewal increases roadmap alignment and upsell runway; we have signals for adding embeddings & dedicated capacity next FY (estimated +$400-600k).

Recommended concession package (my recommendation to limit downside):
1) 20% subscription discount (instead of 25%) for first 12 months only.
2) One-time migration/training credit of $100,000 tied to milestones (50% on signed SOW, 50% on production cutover).
3) Term reset to 12 months on signature with explicit expansion rights at 6 months (no automatic price decrease).
4) SLA addendum to 99.9% with a capped annual service credit equal to 5% of ARR (not cumulative), and a commitment for quarterly ops calls with CS (Marissa to run).

Attachments: redlined amendment, run-rate saving model, excerpt of SOC2 evidence they requested.

Ask: Vivek — can you approve the recommended package above (20% + $100k credit + SLA addendum) so I can go live with legal & finance this afternoon? If not, please indicate which line items require escalation to board or if we should offer a time-limited sweetener (e.g., additional 30 days of free training) instead of increasing the credit.

I will forward the customer's final procurement email after this thread. Time is tight — they asked for a signed amendment by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference

> Team,
> 
> We need executive signoff to close a renewal by end-of-week for Atlas Dynamics (Deal DL-2028-013).

Soojin — thanks for the summary and the attachment set. A few quick clarification items before I sign off:
1) Confirmed ARR at risk: you wrote $600k of committed ARR this coming year — is that net of existing annual credits and committed overages? I need a clear ARR figure that maps to finance.
2) What is the escalation threshold for the SLA credit you propose? If we cap at 5% of ARR, that could be materially large; prefer to define a per-incident or quarterly cap rather than an annual % if possible.
3) Why is the customer insisting on a term reset? Is this a data governance/forecasting ask or strictly procurement alignment?
4) Can finance (David) confirm how a $100k one-time credit will impact our margins and whether it can be reclassified as professional services w/ a clear SOW to protect margin?

If the ARR-at-risk is < $700k and customer has strong expansion signal, I'm inclined to authorize up to your recommended package with two conditions: (A) the credit must be milestone-tied and invoiced as PS where possible, and (B) legal must sign off on a narrowly-scoped SLA addendum with hard caps.

Please reply with the ARR reconciliation and I will issue a short approval email (scope-limited) within the hour.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Vivek — answers inline: 
1) ARR confirmation: $600,000 is the committed subscription ARR for the coming 12-months; it excludes one-off training credits we already delivered this year. The customer also spends ~ $85k/yr on embeddings currently (not contracted for next term).
2) SLA credit structure: propose quarterly cap of 2% of quarterly billed ARR (so annual max ~8% if every quarter missed). I agree that's high — I can ask legal to convert to per-incident credits with a hard annual cap of 5% and no cumulative multiplier.
3) Term reset rationale: procurement wants contract year to align with fiscal year to simplify vendor consolidation — they will not switch mid-term otherwise. They will sign only with a straightforward reset clause.
4) Finance impact: David — can you confirm whether we can classify $100k as PS (in which case margin protected) or if it must be a credit? If PS is okay, we'll attach an SOW that prevents SLA outside scope.

Customer sentiment:
- They view Redwood as the technical leader but procurement is pushing hard on TCO.
- They explicitly named one competitor who is offering 30% off first year + free onboarding (30 days).
- Claire (legal/business contact) said a milestone-tied credit and a clean SLA addendum would be sufficient to sign this week.

If you provisionally approve the package (20% + $100k milestone credit + term reset + legal-limited SLA) I will send the amendment and loop legal/finance.

Thanks,
Soojin

Subject: APPROVED (conditional) — Atlas Dynamics retention package

Soojin / Ben — after reviewing the numbers and customer signals I approve the following conditional package to close DL-2028-013: 
- 20% subscription discount, first 12 months only, applied to the $600k committed ARR.
- One-time migration/training credit capped at $100,000, milestone-tied (50% on signed SOW, 50% on production cutover).
- Term reset to a new 12-month start-on-signature date.
- SLA addendum limited to per-incident credits with an annual cap equal to 5% of ARR; each incident limited and subject to legal review of the annex.

Conditions before signature:
1) Legal must approve the exact SLA language and amendment redline — no open-ended service credit multipliers. Ben, please route to Legal and mark as expedited.
2) Finance (David) to confirm treatment of the $100k credit (PS vs. credit). If reclassified as PS we will tie SOW deliverables and invoice schedule.
3) Deal must include a 90-day rollback clause: if Atlas downgrades usage materially (>=40% drop) within first 6 months, concessions will be subject to clawback per our standard template.

Ben/Marissa — once legal and finance sign off, Soojin you have authority to execute and send the signed amendment to Atlas with the outlined terms. Keep me posted on DocuSign link.

-Vivek
